messages:
bob_acme: Hey team — after we turned on the new Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy for compliance, our Redwood Private agent pods in namespace redwood-private stop completing registration. We see repeated TLS handshake failures and healthcheck 503s.

bob_acme: Agent log sample: 
```
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z ERROR agent connection: controlplane.redwood.internal:443 tls: handshake failure
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z INFO retrying in 5s
2026-03-10T14:02:16Z ERROR agent http: GET /v1/instance/health status=503 body="upstream error"
```

jen_support: thanks for reporting — can you paste `kubectl get networkpolicy -n redwood-private -o yaml` and `kubectl describe pod <agent-pod> -n redwood-private`? also which Calico object did you add (GlobalNetworkPolicy/GNP or default deny NP)?

bob_acme: We added a GNP to default-deny egress for PCI scope. Dump attached (shortened):
```
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: pci-deny-egress
spec:
  order: 100
  selector: "all()"
  types:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - action: Deny
    destination:
      nets: ["0.0.0.0/0"]
```

bob_acme: We intended to be restrictive and forgot to open exceptions for control plane endpoints.

mike_sre: yep that GNP will block agent egress to the control plane. Two quick things to confirm: 1) DNS resolution inside agent pod for controlplane hostname, 2) if ephemeral IPs used by control plane are allowed.

mike_sre: run inside an agent pod: `kubectl exec -n redwood-private <agent-pod> -- sh -c "nslookup controlplane.redwood.internal || true; curl -v https://controlplane.redwood.internal:443/health --max-time 5"`

bob_acme: ran it, output: `nslookup` returns 10.96.0.10 (cluster DNS) then times out; curl: `Failed to connect to controlplane.redwood.internal port 443: Connection timed out`

olivia_runtime: Can you tcpdump egress from agent to see if SYNs leave cluster? `kubectl exec -n redwood-private <agent-pod> -- tcpdump -n -i any port 443` — if you see SYN but no SYN-ACK, likely upstream firewall / GNP drop. If you see no packets, CNI is blocking at host/iptables.

bob_acme: tcpdump shows no outbound SYNs when the GNP is active. When we `kubectl delete gnps pci-deny-egress` immediately the agent starts making outbound connections and registers.

jen_support: that confirms the GNP is the culprit. You need allow rules for the control plane + metrics endpoints and DNS. Two recommended short-term fixes: 1) add an allow rule in your GNP that permits egress from pods in namespace `redwood-private` to the control plane CIDRs/ports, and 2) permit UDP 53 to your kube-dns/coredns cluster IP.

mike_sre: sample minimal Calico GlobalNetworkPolicy exception to add (apply above the deny by lower order):
```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: GlobalNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: redwood-allow-controlplane
spec:
  order: 50
  selector: "k8s_ns == 'redwood-private'"
  types:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    destination:
      nets:
      - 203.0.113.0/24    # control plane CIDR (replace with your CP IPs)
      ports:
      - 443
  - action: Allow
    protocol: UDP
    destination:
      nets:
      - 10.96.0.10/32      # kube-dns cluster IP
      ports:
      - 53
```

olivia_runtime: alternatively, if you can reference FQDNs via egress policy in your policy engine, allow `controlplane.redwood.internal:443` — but Calico GNP doesn't do FQDNs by default, so IP/CIDR is safest.

bob_acme: copied the allow GNP and applied with our real control plane CIDRs, left the core deny for everything else. After apply, agent logs: 
```
2026-03-10T14:11:23Z INFO agent connection: registered instance id=redwood-01
2026-03-10T14:11:23Z INFO healthcheck passed
```

ashley_cs: amazing, thanks for the quick validation. any customer-facing impact while you had it blocked?

bob_acme: we saw ~15m of failed API calls from our app (calls returned 503) and a few in-flight requests retried by our middleware. No billing impact.

jen_support: we'll add a KB doc to support recommended policy exceptions for Private customers running default-deny GNPs. For now I'll mark this as resolved — please reopen if you hit additional blocked ports (metrics, node agent metrics often use 9090/9100).

deploy-bot: ticket #INC-2026-512 created and linked to this thread.

bob_acme: thanks all — closing on our side, and we'll hardcode exception rules into our GNP bootstrap to avoid regressions. :pray:
